description: The inherited exclusive range bound omits a complete final window and does not handle an empty window list.
trigger: Select `--length` equal to the encoded corpus length. More generally, a valid final window is omitted when its start is on the 512-token grid and the row cap has not already been reached. A length greater than the corpus also produces no windows.
expected_behavior: Include a full window that ends exactly at the corpus boundary, and report a clear error when no full window can fit.
actual_behavior: The range excludes start `num_tokens - eval_len`. At equality it yields no rows, so the standalone evaluator's helper calls `torch.cat` on an empty list rather than scoring the one available full row.

verification.description: At length 2048, the range produced no starts for 2048 corpus tokens, one for 2560, and two for 2561.
verification.limits: This checked the range and target counts, not the PyTorch exception.

verification.description: The copied range emits zero starts for 2048 tokens at length 2048, and only start zero for 2560 tokens at length 2048 and stride 512.
verification.limits: Only indexing was run; no tensor concatenation, tokenization, or dataset load was executed.

introductions.rationale: The original standalone helper already used an exclusive stop and concatenated the rows unconditionally. The new length flag makes the width caller-selectable at the observation revision.

finding.description: The copied window loop omits a full window ending exactly at the last token.
finding.trigger: The final valid start `num_tokens - eval_len` is stride-aligned and the row limit would permit it; in particular, the corpus has exactly `eval_len` tokens.
finding.expected_behavior: Include a full window whose end equals the token count; if no complete window fits, report that explicitly.
finding.actual_behavior: The exclusive range stops before that start. At exact corpus/window equality the function passes an empty list to `torch.cat`, so no evaluation rows are produced. The new `main` calls this local helper; the parent search finds separate helpers in `ppl.py`, `model_diff.py`, and `prequant_test.py` with the same range, not calls into the new file.
